content: The hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 plays a critical role in the metabolism of many drugs. Aprepitant, a substance that affects CYP3A4 metabolism, can alter the levels and effects of various medications. Below are detailed interactions and recommendations for specific drugs when co-administered with aprepitant: 1. Cabazitaxel: Aprepitant increases cabazitaxel levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 2. Cabozantinib: Aprepitant raises cabozantinib levels. Exercise caution and monitor. 3. Cannabidiol: Aprepitant elevates cannabidiol levels. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose when used with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 4. Capivasertib: Aprepitant increases capivasertib levels. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the capivasertib dose if co-administered with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 5. Carbamazepine: Aprepitant raises carbamazepine levels by decreasing its metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor plasma levels closely. 6. Cenobamate: Cenobamate decreases aprepitant levels. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Increase the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as needed when co-administered with cenobamate. 7. Cilostazol: Aprepitant increases cilostazol levels. Use caution and monitor. 8. Cinacalcet: Aprepitant raises cinacalcet levels. Exercise caution and monitor. 9. Clomipramine: Aprepitant increases clomipramine levels. Use caution and monitor. 10. Clopidogrel: Aprepitant reduces clopidogrel levels by inhibiting its bioactivation via CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor. 11. Clozapine: Aprepitant elevates clozapine levels. Use caution and monitor. 12. Conivaptan: Aprepitant increases conivaptan levels. Use caution and monitor. 13. Conjugated Estrogens (oral and vaginal): Aprepitant raises conjugated estrogen levels. Use caution and monitor. 14. Cortisone: Aprepitant increases cortisone levels, while cortisone decreases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 15. Crizotinib: Aprepitant raises crizotinib levels, and crizotinib increases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 16. Crofelemer: Crofelemer increases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. Crofelemer inhibits CYP3A4 in the gut but not systemically. 17. Cyclosporine: Aprepitant increases cyclosporine levels, and cyclosporine raises aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 18. Dabrafenib: Dabrafenib decreases aprepitant levels. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 19. Daridorexant: Aprepitant elevates daridorexant levels. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Limit daridorexant to 25 mg per night when used with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 20. Darifenacin: Aprepitant increases darifenacin levels, and darifenacin raises aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 21. Darunavir: Aprepitant raises darunavir levels. Use caution and monitor. 22. Dasatinib: Aprepitant increases dasatinib levels. Use caution and monitor. 23. Deferasirox: Deferasirox decreases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 24. Deflazacort: Aprepitant raises deflazacort levels. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. Reduce deflazacort dose to one-third when used with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 25. Dexamethasone: Aprepitant increases dexamethasone levels, while dexamethasone decreases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 26. DHEA (herbal): DHEA increases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 27. Diazepam: Aprepitant raises diazepam levels. Use caution and monitor. 28. Dichlorphenamide: Both aprepitant and dichlorphenamide decrease serum potassium. Use caution and monitor. 29. Dienogest/Estradiol Valerate: Aprepitant increases levels of these hormones. Monitor for adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache. 30. Diltiazem: Aprepitant raises diltiazem levels. Use caution and monitor. 31. Doxorubicin (including liposomal): Aprepitant increases doxorubicin levels. Use caution and monitor. 32. Dronedarone: Dronedarone raises aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 33. Duvelisib: Duvelisib increases aprepitant levels. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 34. Efavirenz: Efavirenz decreases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 35. Elagolix: Elagolix reduces aprepitant levels. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. 36. Eletriptan: Aprepitant increases eletriptan levels. Use caution and monitor. 37. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF: These drugs increase aprepitant levels. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Cobicistat is a CYP3A4 inhibitor and contraindicated with CYP3A4 substrates that have serious or life-threatening risks at elevated plasma concentrations. 38. Encorafenib: Aprepitant increases encorafenib levels. Use caution and monitor. Encorafenib both inhibits and induces CYP3A4, potentially increasing toxicity or reducing efficacy of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. 39. Erlotinib: Aprepitant raises erlotinib levels. Use caution and monitor. 40. Eslcarbazepine Acetate: Eslcarbazepine decreases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 41. Estradiol: Aprepitant increases estradiol levels. Use caution and monitor. 42. Estrogens (conjugated, synthetic, esterified): Aprepitant raises estrogen levels. Use caution and monitor. Estrogens are CYP3A4 substrates, and their efficacy in hormone replacement therapy may be reduced. 43. Estropipate: Aprepitant increases estropipate levels. Use caution and monitor. 44. Etonogestrel: Aprepitant raises etonogestrel levels. Use caution and monitor. 45. Etoposide: Aprepitant increases etoposide levels. Use caution and monitor. 46. Etravirine: Aprepitant raises etravirine levels, while etravirine decreases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 47. Fedratinib: Fedratinib increases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. Adjust doses of CYP3A4 substrates as necessary. 48. Felodipine: Aprepitant raises felodipine levels. Use caution and monitor. 49. Fesoterodine: Aprepitant increases fesoterodine levels. Use caution and monitor. 50. Finererone: Aprepitant raises finererone levels. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor serum potassium during initiation and dosage adjustments. 51. Fluconazole: Fluconazole increases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 52. Fludrocortisone: Aprepitant raises fludrocortisone levels, while fludrocortisone decreases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 53. Fosamprenavir: Aprepitant increases fosamprenavir levels. Use caution and monitor. 54. Fosphenytoin: Fosphenytoin decreases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 55. Gepirone: Aprepitant raises gepirone levels. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce gepirone dose by 50% when used with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 56. Grapefruit: Grapefruit increases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 57. Griseofulvin: Griseofulvin decreases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 58. Guanfacine: Aprepitant raises guanfacine levels. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce guanfacine dosage to half when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 59. Hydrocortisone: Aprepitant increases hydrocortisone levels, while hydrocortisone decreases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 60. Hydroxyprogesterone Caproate: Aprepitant raises hydroxyprogesterone levels. Use caution and monitor. 61. Ifosfamide: Aprepitant decreases ifosfamide effects. Monitor for neurotoxicity and reduced efficacy. 62. Iloperidone: Aprepitant raises iloperidone levels, and iloperidone increases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 63. Imipramine: Aprepitant increases imipramine levels. Use caution and monitor. 64. Indinavir: Aprepitant raises indinavir levels, and indinavir increases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 65. Irinotecan (including liposomal): Aprepitant increases irinotecan levels. Use caution and monitor. 66. Isavuconazonium Sulfate: Aprepitant decreases isavuconazonium levels. Use caution and monitor. 67. Isoniazid: Isoniazid increases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 68. Istradefylline: Istradefylline raises aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. Reduce doses of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates as needed. 69. Ivosidenib: Aprepitant increases ivosidenib levels. Use caution and monitor for QTc prolongation. 70. Ixabepilone: Aprepitant raises ixabepilone levels. Use caution and monitor. 71. Lapatinib: Aprepitant increases lapatinib levels. Use caution and monitor. 72. Larotrectinib: Larotrectinib raises aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 73. Lefamulin: Aprepitant increases lefamulin levels. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 74. Lenacapavir: Lenacapavir raises aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 75. Letermovir: Letermovir increases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 76. Levamlodipine: Aprepitant raises levamlodipine levels. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 77. Levonorgestrel/Ethinyl Estradiol/Ferrous Bisglycinate: Aprepitant reduces contraceptive efficacy. Use alternative or backup contraception for 28 days after discontinuing enzyme inducers. 78. Linagliptin: Aprepitant raises linagliptin levels. Use caution and consider alternative treatments. 79. Lopinavir: Aprepitant raises lopinavir levels, and lopinavir increases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 80. Loratadine: Aprepitant increases loratadine levels. Use caution and monitor. 81. Lorlatinib: Lorlatinib decreases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 82. Lumateperone: Aprepitant raises lumateperone levels. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce lumateperone dose to 21 mg/day with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 83. Lurasidone: Aprepitant increases lurasidone levels. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce lurasidone starting dose to 20 mg/day and maximum dose to 80 mg/day. 84. Maraviroc: Aprepitant raises maraviroc levels. Use caution and monitor. 85. Marijuana: Marijuana increases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 86. Mavacamten: Aprepitant raises mavacamten levels. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce mavacamten dose with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 87. Mavorixafor: Aprepitant increases mavorixafor levels. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 88. Mefloquine: Aprepitant raises mefloquine levels. Use caution and monitor. 89. Mestranol: Aprepitant increases mestranol levels. Use caution and monitor. 90. Methadone: Aprepitant raises methadone levels. Use caution and monitor. 91. Methylprednisolone: Aprepitant increases methylprednisolone levels, while methylprednisolone decreases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 92. Metronidazole: Metronidazole raises aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 93. Miconazole (vaginal): Miconazole increases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 94. Midazolam: Aprepitant raises midazolam levels. Use caution and monitor. 95. Mifepristone: Aprepitant increases mifepristone levels. Use caution and monitor. 96. Mitotane: Mitotane decreases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. Mitotane is a strong CYP3A4 inducer. 97. Naldemedine: Aprepitant raises naldemedine levels. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 98. Nelfinavir: Aprepitant raises nelfinavir levels, and nelfinavir increases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 99. Nevirapine: Nevirapine decreases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 100. Nicardipine: Aprepitant raises nicardipine levels. Use caution and monitor. 101. Nifedipine: Nifedipine increases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 102. Nilotinib: Aprepitant raises nilotinib levels. Use caution and monitor. 103. Nisoldipine: Aprepitant increases nisoldipine levels. Use caution and monitor. 104. Norgestrel: Aprepitant raises norgestrel levels. Use caution and monitor. 105. Oliceridine: Aprepitant reduces oliceridine levels. Use caution and monitor for respiratory depression and sedation. 106. Oxcarbazepine: Oxcarbazepine decreases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 107. Palbociclib: Aprepitant raises palbociclib levels. Use caution and monitor. 108. Palovarotene: Aprepitant increases palovarotene levels. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Avoid co-administration if possible. 109. Pentobarbital: Pentobarbital decreases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 110. Phenobarbital: Phenobarbital decreases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 111. Phenytoin: Phenytoin decreases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 112. Posaconazole: Posaconazole raises aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 113. Prednisolone: Aprepitant increases prednisolone levels. Use caution and monitor. 114. Prednisone: Aprepitant raises prednisone levels, while prednisone decreases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 115. Primidone: Primidone decreases aprepitant levels. Use caution and monitor. 116. Quetiapine: Aprepitant raises quetiapine levels. Use caution and monitor. 117. Quinidine: Aprepitant increases quinidine levels. Use caution and monitor. This list highlights the importance of monitoring and adjusting therapy when aprepitant is co-administered with other medications, particularly those metabolized by CYP3A4.
